title.narrative: Independent Media Support (IMS) - Independent Media Programme, Iraq 2023-2026
Independent Media Support (IMS) - Program för oberoende media, Irak 2023-2026

description.narrative:
IMS has an overall vision and impact level outcome for the programme. The vision is: A sustainable, inclusive and independent community of media anc civic organisations that supports civil society to actively endorse and promote human rights and political freedoms in Iraq. The impact is of the intervention is a free and independent Iraqi media and civil society support and enable civic activity and promote human rights and political freedoms in Iraq.
The proposed programme is to operate within the following three outcome areas and objectives for 2023-2025:
Outcome 1 Public Interest Content and Media Media actors produce ethical, inclusive and gender sensitive content to Iraqi audiences that counters mis/disinformation, raises awareness of critical issues, and enhances public accountability.
Outcome 2 Enabling Environment: Safety Media actors, journalists, and human rights defenders, particularly women, are better protected and enjoy safer working environments in Iraq.
Outcome 3 Enabling Environment: Policy and Law Media and Freedom of Expression (FoE) actors, including women, advocate and contribute to advancing human rights and accountability for the media workers and journalists.

Det övergripande målet med insatsen är att stärka oberoende media i Irak genom att bidra till kapacitetsuppbyggnad i faktabaserad och grävande journalistik som möjliggör ansvarsutkrävande och som anknyter till nyheter som är av intresse i den lokala kontexten.
Stödet ska vidare möjliggöra offentlig dialog i frågor om mänskliga rättigheter, jämställdhet och minoriteters rättigheter.
Insatsen inkluderar 12 partners; sju medieaktörer och fem civilsamhällesorganisationer. Mediapartners kommer att erbjudas utbildningar i faktabaserad och grävande journalistik, intern organisationsuppbyggnad och diversifiering av den finansiella portföljen. Övriga partners kommer arbeta med stärkande av säkerhetsåtgärder för journalister, övervakning av kränkningar av journalister och påverkansarbete kring bristerna i rådande lagstiftning om yttrandefrihet, pressfrihet och strafflagstiftning. Insatsen bidrar till OECD DACs kod 15153 om stöd till media och informationsfrihet då syftet med insatsen är att bidra till att journalister inom oberoende media framställer faktabaserad journalistik och fri från disinformation. Sommaren 2024 beslöt Sveriges regering att fasa ut allt bilateralt bistånd till Irak och därför avslutades denna insats 30 juni 2025.

The overall objective of the programme is to strengthen public interest media to produce ethical, diverse, accountable, and inclusive public interest content. The contribution will also enable public debate on human rights, accountability and the advancement of positive social, political and cultural change.
The contribution will allow forwarding of funds to 12 partners, seven media actors and five civil society organisations. Media partners will be offered training public interest content and media and disinformation while the civil society organisation will be doing advocacy on increasing an enabling environment for journalists in Iraq, by advancing human rights and accountability for the media workers and journalists. The contribution is linked to the OECD DAC's code 15153 since it aims to support journalists connected to independent media to develop media content that is fact-based and free from disinformation. In July 2024 the Swedish government decided to phase out all bilateral development cooperation with Iraq. Therefore, this contribution ended on 30 June 2025.

sector.narrative: Media and free flow of information

description.narrative:
The support to International Media Support (IMS) programme in Iraq contributed to strengthened public interest media in Iraq through flexible funding and tailored capacity development for five media and two advocacy partners. The programme contributed to improved editorial quality, digital capacity, and organisational resilience, contributing to more independent and effective journalism.
Key Results
Stronger media capacity and audience engagement Partners enhanced their use of audience data, enabling more targeted and responsive content strategies. This contributed to a 27% increase in online audiences from 2023 to 2024 and shifts toward younger audiences through digital storytelling and platform diversification.
High-impact investigative journalism Partners produced over 4,200 content pieces (2023-2025), with investigations exposing corruption, organised crime, and governance failures. Reporting contributed to public debate and concrete actions, including regulatory changes, improved safety measures, and increased institutional scrutiny.
Environmental journalism as a growing strength Environmental reporting evolved into a core area, linking climate and pollution issues to governance, health, and livelihoods. Investigations led to tangible outcomes such as closure of illegal facilities and new regulatory measures, while audience engagement and institutional recognition increased.
Improved gender equality and inclusion Partners advanced gender-sensitive reporting and internal practices through audits, policies, and targeted content. This contributed to more inclusive narratives and strengthened organisational approaches to gender and safety.
Skills development and new talent A structured fellowship programme strengthened the skills and employability of emerging journalists, with several participants transitioning into professional roles.
Safety and support systems IMS and partners adopted a holistic safety approach, including legal aid, psychosocial support, and organisational safeguarding. Over 180 journalists received legal assistance, and partners improved internal safety practices despite budget constraints.
Policy and advocacy contributions The programme supported monitoring of press freedom violations and advocacy for legal reforms, including progress on access to information legislation. However, results in this area remain less clearly defined.
Limitations
Evidence of behavioural change and audience reach is limited in some areas, particularly documentary production Policy-level outcomes are difficult to attribute and insufficiently documented Continued security and political constraints limit broader systemic impact
Overall Assessment
The programme demonstrates strong results in media capacity, investigative journalism, and environmental reporting, with clear contributions to public debate and accountability. However, evidence gaps and contextual constraints limit the ability to fully assess long-term impact, particularly at the policy level.
